back: If the stack is full, report overflow; otherwise TopPointer ← TopPointer + 1 and store the item at Stack[TopPointer].
If the stack is empty, report underflow; otherwise take Stack[TopPointer], then TopPointer ← TopPointer - 1.
Overflow: pushing onto a full stack. Underflow: popping from an empty stack.
If Count = QueueSize the queue is full; otherwise RearPointer ← MOD(RearPointer, QueueSize) + 1, store the item, Count ← Count + 1.
If Count = 0 the queue is empty; otherwise take Queue[FrontPointer], FrontPointer ← MOD(FrontPointer, QueueSize) + 1, Count ← Count - 1.
Pointers wrap from the last place to the first, so freed places are reused; a count shows full or empty.
In a circular queue the pointers look the same when the queue is full and when it is empty.
Pseudocode arrays here start at 1, Python lists at 0, so pointer values differ by one.
Stack: undo, browser history, call stack, reversing. Queue: print jobs, buffers, waiting lines.
